HPLC is the gold standard for measuring cortisol levels in critically ill patients.
the diagnosis of relative or absolute adrenal insufficiency should be confirmed by a second assay and that HPLC is the preferred method.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of immunoassays to measure plasma total cortisol in critically ill patients is not recommended.
the use of HPLC is recommended in order to obtain more precise results and to reduce the risk of false positive diagnosis of adrenal insuficiency.
immunoassay estimation for total plasma cortisol in patients with sepsic is highly variable and may lead to incorrect diagnosis and treatment of relative adrenal insuficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are significant differences between the assays and that the diagnosis of adrenal dysfunction should be confirmed by a second test.
the use of a single immunoassay to determine the diagnosis of relative or absolute adrenal insufficiency may be problematic.
